elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 10.5: "This Agreement shall be governed and construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of New York ... without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws." Choice-of-law wording is untouched by the edit.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York shall have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits of any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement, provided that either Party may seek temporary injunctive relief in any other court of competent jurisdiction." Both state and federal courts are named, exclusivity attaches to the merits, and the only other-forum carve-out is the customary temporary injunctive relief exception, which preserves the exclusive merits forum.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The governing law remains the State of New York; no Delaware, California, or England and Wales law is selected. This is expected because the proposal targets the preferred level, which is more favourable.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: The inserted forum is New York County, New York, not Delaware, California, or London. Again consistent with pursuing the preferred level rather than the fallback.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: New York law is already selected in retained Section 10.5, and the single inserted sentence supplies the missing exclusive New York County forum for the merits with only a temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out.

The fallback level is not met (law and forum are New York, not Delaware/California/England and Wales), but completeness at either level suffices, and the preferred level is the stronger customer position.

Minimality is satisfied: the original choice-of-law sentence is preserved verbatim with no deletion or paraphrase, and the addition is a concise insertion of the absent forum term only. No survival tail, expense allocation, procedural steps, fee-shifting, service-of-process, jury-waiver, or other boilerplate extras were added, and no requirement outside the GOVLAW checklist appears.

Intent is preserved: notices, assignment, waiver, severability, survival, entire agreement, and headings provisions are untouched; the insertion creates no undefined term ("Party" is a document-level term) and no dangling cross-reference, and there is no retained arbitration, alternate-venue, or dispute-resolution sentence that would contradict the new exclusive forum.

Deterministic checks are corroborated on substance: the governing law sits within the accepted set, the forum operation renders as operative language rather than a promise in the comment, and element coverage at the preferred level is complete.

Finding status "deviation" is appropriate: the document lacked any forum or venue provision, so it failed the fallback forum element as well as the preferred one, justifying a redline rather than a compliant classification. Severity remains medium per the rule.
